findings.location: Scene 2, line 629 (advisory, not a fail driver)
findings.passage: She stayed where she was, going round again.
findings.problem: This participle contradicts the main clause. 'Stayed where she was' means she didn't move, and 'going round again' is her walking the ward round. Last round's sweep of sequential participials missed it. It closes the beat where she chooses the wards over going down to Sylvanas, so the reader stops on it.
findings.fix: Keep both halves but make the meaning clear: 'She stayed, and went round again.' Or keep the choice in the sentence: 'She didn't go down. She went round again.'

findings.passage: she came at it from one side and slid off, coming at it from another and sliding off again
findings.problem: This is a sequential participle. She tries the second side after sliding off the first, so the ', coming' wrongly makes the two attempts sound simultaneous. It is the same pattern r1 cleared everywhere else.
findings.fix: 'she came at it from one side and slid off, and came at it from another and slid off again'. The repeated 'and' copies her repeated attempts and adds a compound join (compound is at 9.7%, so there is room).

findings.passage: Lyriel's hand came across from the right and took the cheek-strap, Lyriel not so much as turning her head.
findings.problem: This gives agency to a body part when the real actor is in the sentence, and then names Lyriel a second time in a stiff trailing clause to fix it. It is the same pattern r1 fixed at 739, and here it is in the opening paragraph.
findings.fix: 'Lyriel reached across from the right and took the cheek-strap without turning her head.'

findings.passage: She got down, doing it badly, as she did it every time / Her breath sobbing in her chest by the yew, she shouldered the chapel door open. / Every one of them had thinned—not as far as his, though every one, while she had been down in the dark with a jar and a boy.
findings.problem: Three clumsy sentences. At 149, 'doing it badly' repeats 'got down' and only adds a participle. At 997 the opening clause puts her sobbing breath at the yew, while the main verb happens at the door, so place and action don't line up. At 1003 the dash and 'though every one' make the reader parse it twice. At 1179, 'got up badly, as she always got up' is a deliberate echo of 149, and it lands better if 149 is just as clean.
findings.fix: 149: 'She got down badly, as she did every time, the staff sliding...'. 997: 'By the yew her breath was sobbing in her chest. She shouldered the chapel door open.' 1003: 'Every one of them had thinned while she was down in the dark with a jar and a boy. None as far as his, but every one.'

findings.passage: Cyndia a pace behind and to the left of them with her hand resting near her quiver. / Cyndia stood a pace behind her and to the left, where she had stood at Brask's shoulder in the lane, resting her hand near her quiver.
findings.problem: 593 already points back to the lane, so it doesn't need to repeat the exact words 'resting ... near her quiver' as well. The r1 participial pass created this near-verbatim echo.
findings.fix: At 593 drop the trailing clause or change the detail: '...where she had stood at Brask's shoulder in the lane.' Sylvanas reads Cyndia's eyes going right (see the voice sheet), so 'her eyes going to the right and back' would fit if a detail is wanted.
